Tired of paying LLM token taxes and waiting seconds just to get a simple classification or JSON flag? 🛑 Say hello to Laya—a non-autoregressive decision engine built for high-throughput production pipelines.

🚀 Laya delivers typed multilingual AI decisions in a single forward pass—no text generation, no parsing headaches, and zero hallucination risks. 

⚡️ What problem does it solve?
Traditional LLMs are slow, expensive, and unpredictable for structured decision-making tasks. Laya evaluates typed questions like choices, scores, and boolean flags over any text or JSON document in roughly 33 milliseconds on a T4 GPU. 

🔥 Key Features:
• Single Forward Pass: Evaluates multiple typed questions simultaneously in ~33ms without text generation or post-processing parsers.
• Intelligent Multi-Model Router: Automatically detects scripts and languages in sub-milliseconds to dispatch requests to the optimal checkpoint.
• RL Calibration (RLCD): Trained with scoring rules to produce statistically meaningful confidence scores for reliable automated threshold gating.
• Workflow Presets: Ships pre-tuned for model routing, prompt guardrails, content moderation, and support ticket triage.

💡 Developer Value:
Drop Laya into your stack to replace heavy, slow LLM calls for classification and routing. Because it provides statistically calibrated confidence scores, your team can automate straight-through processing for high-confidence decisions while gracefully routing edge cases to human reviewers—drastically slashing compute costs and latency.

👉 Check out the repo and start building faster today:
https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya

Tired of bloated creative suites and subscription lock-in? 🛑 Say hello to Compositor—a full-featured, open-source native Mac image editor built completely from scratch in Swift. 🍏✨

The Problem: 
Modern creative software is heavy, expensive, and trapped behind endless subscription walls. For developers and designers who just want a high-performance native tool for compositing and post-processing without the massive resource overhead of Electron apps, options have been frustratingly limited.

The Solution: 
Compositor delivers lightning-fast, native macOS performance tailored for workflows familiar to Photoshop users—completely free and open source. 🚀

Key Features You'll Love:
🔹 Comprehensive layer & mask management (folders, blend modes, opacity, clipping masks, adjustment layers, and non-destructive transforms)
🔹 Advanced selection & retouching tools (content-aware fill, spot healing brushes, clone stamping, and geometric marquees)
🔹 Complete filter pipeline with live previews, color adjustments, and multi-tab project management using standard Photoshop-style shortcuts
🔹 Built entirely in Swift and Xcode for optimal native performance

Why Developers Need This on Their Radar:
Beyond being an incredible daily-driver tool, Compositor serves as a stellar reference architecture for building complex, high-performance native macOS applications in Swift. Audit the codebase, extend it with custom plugins or automated batch-processing scripts, or fork the Xcode project to build your own domain-specific image processing tools and asset generators. 🛠️💻

Check out the repo, explore the architecture, and drop a star to support open-source native tooling:
https://github.com/robbietilton/Compositor

Tired of burning through your API budget just to watch an AI agent slowly stare at screenshots? 💸

Meet typesafe-computer-use: an open-source tool that runs AI computer-use loops 150x cheaper and up to 40x faster than frontier multimodal models! 🚀

The Problem:
Traditional desktop automation relies on sending full, raw screenshots to massive vision-language models for every single step. It is painfully slow, wildly expensive, and prone to high latency. 

The Solution:
This project drives a Mac toward any user-defined goal in plain English by combining native macOS accessibility trees, deterministic OCR caching, and lightweight classification. Instead of brute-forcing pixels, it reads the screen deterministically, queries a small decision model for the next action, and only calls heavy models when free-text generation is actually required. 

Key Features:
⚡ Ultra-Low Cost & Speed: Executes steps for about 1/50th of a cent with sub-second decision latencies.
🧠 Smart OCR Caching: Compares screen captures in 256px tiles to reuse unchanged text blocks and cut processing overhead.
🔍 Hybrid Extraction: Merges native macOS accessibility APIs with Vision OCR to accurately target buttons, icons, and text fields.
🛠️ Deterministic Fallback: Relies on local structured choices and parsing modules instead of expensive zero-shot inference.

Perfect for AI engineers, automation developers, and technical founders building production-grade desktop testing, CI/CD UI validation, or cost-effective personal assistants. 

Check out the repo and start scaling your desktop agents economically today:
https://github.com/awlevin/typesafe-computer-use

Stop waiting on cloud APIs for your real-time AI agents. 🚀

Run open-weight typed decision models natively on Apple Silicon at single-digit millisecond latencies without PyTorch or cloud APIs.

If you are building high-performance local AI pipelines, you know the pain of standard autoregressive text generation and heavy JSON parsing just to get a simple classification or score. 

`mizorewww/laya-mlx` is a native Apple Silicon MLX runtime built for open-weight typed decision models. Instead of generating text token-by-token, it uses a bidirectional forward pass that directly outputs structured classifications, rubric scores, and probabilities.

🔥 Key Features & Developer Value:
• Ultra-low inference latency: Delivers a median of 7.4 ms to 13.4 ms per decision locally on Apple hardware.
• Direct structured outputs: Bypasses text generation entirely to output choices and probabilities straight from decision heads.
• Lightweight & independent: Fully leverages Apple MLX and Hugging Face Rust tokenizers without depending on PyTorch or heavier Transformers runtimes.
• Optimized architectures: Supports ModernBERT-large and mmBERT-base with robust compilation and prefix-reuse pathways.

Whether you are engineering real-time game loops requiring sub-15ms decision cycles or automating high-throughput support routing and intent classification locally, this cuts out cloud costs, privacy risks, and heavy runtime dependencies.

👉 Check out the repo and start building today:
https://github.com/mizorewww/laya-mlx

Ever wanted to query, decrypt, and export your local WeChat data straight from the terminal without breaking a sweat or disabling system security? 

Most developers trying to access local messaging data hit a wall: you are forced to do heavy pre-decryption, fiddle with fragile scripts, or bypass critical system integrity protections just to read your own chat history. 

Enter `wx-cli-again`—a zero-dependency Rust CLI utility built for high-performance data extraction. It lets you securely query, decrypt, and export chat history, sessions, contacts, groups, favorites, and encrypted attachments right from your command line.

Here is why developers and AI engineers are adding it to their toolkits:

⚡ Sub-Millisecond Caching: Features a persistent daemon that dynamically decrypts SQLite databases based on file modification times.
🔍 Cross-Platform Key Extraction: Comprehensive pipelines utilizing memory scanning and dynamic debugging hooks (LLDB) for macOS, Linux, and Windows.
🤖 AI-Ready JSON Output: Automated metadata wrappers (freshness, source tracking, and stable identity fields) optimized for seamless integration with coding assistants like Claude Code and Cursor.
📂 Attachment Decryption: Built-in support for legacy XOR, V1 AES, and platform-derived V2 AES image decoding.

Use it to feed local chat archives as RAG context for your custom AI coding assistants, or simply automate the backup, search, and migration of your personal archives. 

Check out the repo and drop a star if you find it useful:
https://github.com/jackwener/wx-cli-again
